rationale: Wikipedia's page on the 2010 Toronto mayoral election has a candidate profile headed Abdullah-Baquie Ghazi, and its results table gives Abdullah-Baquie Ghazi 2,761 votes, the record's 2010 mayoral run. The profile says 'Ghazi ran for councillor from Ward 28 (Toronto Centre) in 2006 and received 3.3% of the vote.' The record's 2006 Ward 28 council run, printed 'Baquie Ghazi', has 440 of 13,439 votes (3.3 per cent) and is the only Ghazi in that race, so it is the run the profile describes. The profile places the run printed 'Baquie Ghazi' in the career of the candidate printed 'Abdullah-Baquie Ghazi', which accounts for the 2006 printing leaving out the first part of the hyphenated given name. No source found describes the held 2018 TDSB Ward 10 run printed 'Baquie Ghazi', and it stays held. The 2006 Ward 28 council run and the 2010 mayoral run are joined.

No source describes either candidate, so the join rests on same-office continuity. The Toronto Star's school board results of 14 November 1997 give Salvatore (Scott) Cusimano second of three, with 4,652 votes, for Toronto Catholic District School Board trustee in Ward 5, and the City's Vote 2000 results give Scott Cusimano fourth of eight, with 1,400 votes, for the same board's Ward 5 at the next general election. The 1997 listing prints Scott beside his given name Salvatore, so the two printed names are forms of one name. The release has no boundaries for these wards, but its records place both in central North York. The 1997 Ward 5 winner, Donald Clune, and the third-placed candidate, Lucy Kopach, had run in 1994 for the Metropolitan Separate School Board in Ward 13 (North York Wards 6, 8, 10 and 12) and Ward 14 (North York Wards 9, 11, 13 and 14). The councillors elected in 1994 for North York Wards 6, 8, 9, 11 and 13 stood in 2000 in city wards 16, 25, 23, 23 and 24. The City's 2003 results give the Catholic board's Ward 5 as city wards 15, 16, 23, 24 and 25. Wikipedia's article on the 2000 election says the board's twelve trustee wards that year each comprised two to six of the 44 city wards first used then, and the three Catholic trustees elected in 2000 who ran again in 2003 did so in wards of the same number. North York Wards 6, 8, 9, 11 and 13, whose 1994 councillors stood in 2000 in the city wards of the later Ward 5, are five of the eight North York wards in the 1997 Ward 5's area, and the Willowdale wards 23 and 24 alone make up about two-fifths of the area of the five city wards, so the two trustee wards overlap by well over a fifth of each. The overlap is inferred from these runs because the release has no boundaries for the 1997 and 2000 trustee wards. Cusimano is an uncommon surname. The only other Person with it in the release is Gus Cusimano, a council candidate in 2010 and 2014, and no other candidate printed as Scott or Salvatore Cusimano ran. The 1997 and 2000 Catholic board Ward 5 runs are joined as one Person.

The Toronto Star's story of 26 October 1993 on the York South—Weston race describes the Progressive Conservative candidate Tony Figliano as 42 and a land development consultant, and says his campaign collapsed. That is the 1993 York South—Weston Progressive Conservative run, third of eleven with 2,508 votes, for which Elections Canada gives the occupation consultant. One sentence of the story prints the name as Tory Figliano; it describes the same Progressive Conservative candidate, whom the story elsewhere calls Tony Figliano, so it refers to this run. The Star's York Centre stories of 25 May and 3 June 1997 describe the Progressive Conservative candidate as 46 and a land development consultant, and call him Tony Figliano in the first and Anthony Figliano in the second. That is the 1997 York Centre Progressive Conservative run printed Anthony Figliano, third of eight with 3,323 votes. The same occupation is given for both runs, the ages agree, and the 1997 coverage uses both forms of the name for one candidate, which accounts for the different printed names. The other Figlianos in the release, Nick in 1994 and Matteo in 2010, have other given names. The 1997 Toronto Catholic District School Board Ward 10 run printed Anthony Figliano is not part of this join and stays held. The 1993 York South—Weston run and the 1997 York Centre run are joined as one Person.

The Toronto Star's Willowdale candidate profiles of 22 October 1993 describe the National Party candidate Shelley Goldstein as 'a professional actor and producer' and refer to her as she, which is the record's 1993 National Party run in Willowdale. Elections Canada gives her occupation for that run as performer, and gives the same occupation for the Green candidate printed 'Shel Goldstein' in Eglinton—Lawrence in 2004, the record's 2004 run. The York Guardian's report of 25 June 2004 on an Eglinton-Lawrence candidates' night names the Green candidate Shel Goldstein and also refers to her as she. Shel is the usual short form of Shelley. The 1993 Willowdale run and the 2004 Eglinton—Lawrence run are joined.

Wikipedia's article on the 2006 Toronto mayoral election describes the mayoral candidate Lee Romano as a Toronto businesswoman who founded the Consumer's Guide to Insurance and had written a column in the Toronto Star's Wheels section since 2005 under the name Lee Romanov. Wikipedia's article on the 2006 municipal election lists her in the mayoral results as Lee Romanov with 3,108 votes, the total the City gives for the 2006 run printed 'Lee Romano', so the source gives both forms of the surname for the 2006 candidate. Wikipedia's article on the 2014 mayoral election lists Lee Romanov with 271 votes, as in the City's results, and no source describes that candidate further. The two runs are for mayor, with one general election (2010) between, under a name that is uncommon in either form, that no other Person in the release has and that no other candidate used, so same-office continuity applies. The 2006 and 2014 mayoral runs are joined as one Person.

Elections Canada's 1993 record gives the New Democratic Party candidate in Scarborough—Agincourt, printed 'Joe José Perez' (fourth of nine, 942 votes), as a mechanical engineer. The Catholic Register's profiles of Toronto Catholic District School Board candidates, published on 20 October 2010, list Jose Perez in Ward 3 (city wards 7 and 12) with Matteo Figliano and Sal Piccininni, the other two candidates in the 2010 Ward 3 result, and give his qualification as 'Mechanical Engineer by the Barcelona Polytechnic Institute (1968)'. The profile also says he was born in Barcelona, received an award from the former City of York in 1988 and sat on the board of the Federation of Catholic Parents Teachers Association of Ontario in 1991 and 1992. The profession given in both sources is the fact that links the runs. The 1993 record prints the nickname Joe beside the given name José, which accounts for the 2010 record printing the name as Jose Perez. The name is common and the runs are 17 years apart, for different offices in different parts of the city, so the link rests on the matching profession; no other Jose or Joe Perez in the release is described with a different occupation. The 1993 House of Commons run in Scarborough—Agincourt and the 2010 Toronto Catholic District School Board Ward 3 run are joined as one Person.

The Globe and Mail's report on the 2010 Ward 15 race says that Josh Colle, son of MPP Mike Colle, was elected city councillor in Ward 15, replacing Howard Moscoe, and gives the City's unofficial results as 6,668 votes for Mr. Colle to 5,399 for the runner-up Rob Davis. Those totals match the 2010 Ward 15 run printed Josh Colle. The same report calls him "the former Toronto Catholic School Board trustee". The City's 2000 results give Joshua Colle as the elected trustee for Toronto Catholic District School Board Ward 5 (first of eight, 3,409 votes), and no other Colle won a seat on that board in the release before 2010; Larry Colle's only run, in 2014, was a loss. The office held therefore ties the Globe's Josh Colle to the trustee run, and the Globe uses Josh, the common short form of Joshua, for the man who held the seat won under the full name. The 2000 Catholic board Ward 5 run and the 2010 and 2014 Ward 15 council runs are joined as one Person.

Wikipedia's biography of David John Johnson, a former mayor of East York, says he entered the Ontario legislature for Don Mills in an April 1993 by-election and was easily re-elected in the 1995 provincial election, which matches the 1995 Don Mills win printed 'Dave Johnson' (14,897 votes). It says he ran in Don Valley East in the 1999 provincial election and was defeated by Liberal David Caplan, which matches the 1999 run printed 'DAVE JOHNSON', second to Caplan with 17,955 votes. The biography puts the 1999 margin at about 2,500 where the official count gives 3,038, but the riding, year, party and winner agree. It says he was the Conservative candidate in Don Valley East in the 2004 federal election and lost to Liberal Yasmin Ratansi by more than 10,000 votes, which matches the 2004 run printed 'David Johnson', second with 11,206 votes to Ratansi's 21,864. The biography gives the runs printed with the nickname Dave and the run printed as David to one man, which accounts for the different printed names. The Election Prediction Project's 2004 Don Valley East page lists the Conservative candidate as David Johnson, and its reader comments call him Dave Johnson, the former Ontario education minister who lost the riding in 1999. The 1995 Don Mills and 1999 Don Valley East Ontario legislature runs and the 2004 Don Valley East House of Commons run are joined as one Person.

The Toronto Star's article of 10 January 2002 on school trustee Sam Basra ('Notice barred Basra's 2000 election bid', by Philip Mascoll and Bruce DeMara) says Basra 'also ran for the Progressive Conservatives in the riding of Etobicoke North in the 1997 federal election as Sam Basran', and that he dropped the 'n' from the name Basran he used in 1997 and won a board seat as Sam Basra. The trustee is the record's 2000 Toronto District School Board Ward 1 (Etobicoke North) winner, printed 'Sam Basra', who is the only Basra in the release. The federal run is the record's 1997 Progressive Conservative run in Etobicoke North, printed 'Sam Basran', third of seven. The article names both runs and gives both spellings of the surname for one man, which accounts for the different printed names. It also mentions a 1997 municipal run as Sam Basran, which is not in the release. The 2000 TDSB Ward 1 run and the 1997 Etobicoke North federal run are joined.

The Toronto Star of 23 May 1997, reporting on the race for the North York Humber seats on the new city council, says that North York Ward 2 Councillor Gina Severino has registered, and the Star's arts report card of 16 October 1997 lists Gina Severino among the candidates in Ward 6 North York-Humber. The City's 1997 results print the third-placed candidate in Ward 6 (North York Humber), with 6,875 votes, as Gina Serverino. She is the only candidate in that race with a similar name, so the Star's articles describe her run and spell the name Severino. The City's 1994 results give Gina Severino as elected to North York council in Ward 2, the office the Star says the 1997 candidate held, and the Star's 1994 North York council profiles describe her as a legal assistant. The 1994 North York Ward 2 and 1997 Ward 6 council runs are joined as one Person.

The Local's guide to the 2022 Ward 2 (Etobicoke Centre) council race, published 15 September 2022 and last updated 11 October 2022, profiles the council candidate Catherine Habus, who placed third of five with 2,318 votes. It says she is an analyst and that during the provincial election she ran for MPP in Etobicoke Centre for the New Blue Party of Ontario and came fifth with 1,117 votes. That is the June 2022 Etobicoke Centre run printed CATHY HABUS, fifth of eight with 1,117 votes. The guide names both runs, and it uses the full given name Catherine for the run printed with the short form Cathy, which accounts for the different printed names. No one else in the release has the surname Habus. The June 2022 Etobicoke Centre provincial run and the October 2022 Ward 2 council run are joined as one Person.

Wikipedia's article on the Go Vegan party gives its leader as Paulo Figueiras and lists him as the party's candidate in Trinity—Spadina at the 2014 Ontario election (308 votes, 0.53 per cent, sixth of seven) and in University—Rosedale at the 2018 election (106 votes, 0.21 per cent, eighth of nine). The 2018 row matches the record's run printed 'Paulo Figueiras'. The 2014 row is the record's Go Vegan run in Trinity—Spadina printed 'PAUL FIGUEIRAS': the riding, year, party and placing match, and the record's 307 votes are the 0.53 per cent of valid votes that the article gives. The article prints the 2014 candidate as Paulo, the form printed for the 2018 run, and Paul is the English form of Paulo, which accounts for the different printed names. The two runs also meet same-office continuity: the same office and party at consecutive general elections, an uncommon surname with no other Figueiras in the release, and ridings that overlap by about half of University—Rosedale. The 2014 Trinity—Spadina run and the 2018 University—Rosedale run are joined.

No source describes either candidate, so the join rests on same-office continuity. David Searle ran for Toronto City Council in Ward 6 (Etobicoke-Lakeshore) in 2003 and 2010, placing ninth of ten and sixth of six, and Dave Searle ran in the same ward in 2014, placing twelfth of twelve. All three runs used the 44-ward map, whose Ward 6 boundary did not change between 2003 and 2014, and there was no general election between the 2010 and 2014 runs. Council races have no parties. Searle is an uncommon surname, no one else in the release has it, and no other candidate of the name ran in these elections. Dave is the common short form of David, so the printed names are evidently forms of one name. The 2014 Ward 6 run is joined to the Person holding the 2003 and 2010 Ward 6 runs.

Wikipedia's list of Communist Party of Canada (Marxist-Leninist) candidates in the 2006 federal election has an entry on the party's candidate in Bramalea—Gore—Malton, Chilelli. Its electoral record lists his 1997 run in Davenport (250 votes, sixth of eight) and his 2000 run in Eglinton—Lawrence (164 votes, sixth of seven), both for the Marxist-Leninist Party, as in Elections Canada's results. The entry says he joined the party in 1996 as a graduate student at the University of Toronto and was later a philosophy teacher, and Elections Canada lists the 1997 candidate as a student and the 2000 candidate as a teacher. Elections Canada prints the 1997 candidate as Francesco Chilelli and the 2000 candidate as Frank Chilelli. The entry assigns both runs to one man and cites his 1998 University of Toronto thesis under the name Frank Chilelli, and Frank is the usual English form of Francesco. No one else with the surname is in the release. The 1997 Davenport and 2000 Eglinton—Lawrence runs are joined as one Person.

Gerry Altobello's Wikipedia biography says that after amalgamation he ran for Toronto City Council in Ward 13, where the two candidates with the most votes were elected, that he was elected with Brian Ashton, and that 'Fellow Scarborough city councillor Fred Johnson came in third.' The official 1997 Ward 13 (Scarborough Bluffs) result has Ashton first, Altobello second and Fred Johnston third with 11,265 votes, so the biography describes this run and prints the surname as Johnson. The City's archived 1994 results show Fred Johnson elected to Scarborough council in Ward 7 with 6,545 votes to Ed Green's 1,675, and Brian Ashton's Wikipedia biography names Fred Johnson as his successor in Scarborough's Ward 7 seat, so Fred Johnson was a sitting Scarborough councillor at the 1997 election. The office held, which the biography gives for the 1997 run and the official results give for the 1994 run, links the two, and the biography's use of the 1994 spelling for the 1997 run accounts for the record printing it as Johnston. No other Fred Johnson or Fred Johnston appears in the release. Ed Green, the only other 1994 Ward 7 candidate, also ran in the 1997 Ward 13 race. The 1994 Scarborough Ward 7 council run and the 1997 Toronto Ward 13 council run are joined as one Person.

No source describes either candidate, so the join rests on same-office continuity. Both runs are for trustee on the Toronto Catholic District School Board in Ward 4, in 1997 and 2003, with one general election (2000) between them, and trustee races have no parties. The City's archived 1997 results describe Ward 4 as Toronto Wards 7 and 8, the Black Creek and North York Spadina wards, and the City's 2003 results make Ward 4 city wards 8, 9 and 10 in York West and York Centre. Peter Li Preti, Maria Augimeri and Mike Feldman, elected to council in Black Creek and North York Spadina in 1997, held the new Wards 8, 9 and 10 in 2000 and 2003, and Mary Cicogna won trustee Ward 4 in both 1997 and 2003, so the two wards cover much of the same area. Cossidente is a rare surname, no one else in the release has it, and no other candidate of the name ran in either election. The 1997 record, from the Toronto Star's results, prints the candidate as 'Settimio (Sam) Cossidente', and the City's archived 1997 results print the same run as 'Sam Cossidente' with the same 1,342 votes, which accounts for the 2003 record's 'Sam Cossidente'. The 1997 and 2003 Toronto Catholic District School Board Ward 4 runs are joined as one Person.

Wikipedia's biography of Bas Balkissoon says that he sat on Scarborough council for Ward 13 from 1988 until amalgamation, that he was elected to the amalgamated Toronto City Council in 1997, and that he was councillor for Ward 18 Scarborough Malvern from 1998 to 2000 and for Ward 41 Scarborough-Rouge River from 2000 to 2005, before sitting for Scarborough—Rouge River in the Ontario legislature from 2005. Wikipedia's results for the 1997 election list Bas Balkissoon second in Ward 18 Scarborough Malvern with 10,745 votes. The City's 1997 results print the same candidate, second of nine with 10,745 votes and elected to one of the ward's two seats, as Bas Balkisson, and no other candidate in that race has a similar name. The biography, Wikipedia's 1997 results and the official records of his other runs all spell the surname Balkissoon, so Balkisson is a misspelling in the City's 1997 results. The 1997 Ward 18 run is joined to the Person holding his 1994 Scarborough Ward 13, 2000 and 2003 Ward 41, and Ontario legislature runs.

Wikipedia's biography under the title Dan Goldstick opens "Daniel "Danny" Goldstick (born 1940) is a Canadian philosopher, writer and political activist" and says he is a professor emeritus at the University of Toronto. Its electoral record lists the 2000 federal election in Toronto Centre—Rosedale with 121 votes and the 2004 federal election in Toronto Centre with 106 votes, both won by Bill Graham. These match the 2000 Communist run printed Danny Goldstick (eighth of nine, 121 votes) and the 2004 Communist run printed Dan Goldstick (sixth of eight, 106 votes), and Elections Canada gives the candidate as a university teacher in both years. The biography gives Daniel, Danny and Dan for one man, which accounts for the two printed forms, and no other Goldstick appears in the release. The same record lists the 1993 York South—Weston run, printed Danny Red Goldstick, which is already on the Danny Goldstick Person. The 2004 Toronto Centre run is joined to the Person holding the 1993 York South—Weston and 2000 Toronto Centre—Rosedale runs.

The York Guardian of 30 April 2004 says Stephen Halicki had won the Conservative Party of Canada nomination and that he ran for the York South-Weston seat in the previous fall's provincial election as a Progressive Conservative and lost to the Liberal incumbent Joe Cordiano. That describes the record's 2004 Conservative run in York South—Weston, printed 'Stephen Halicki', and its 2003 Progressive Conservative run there, printed 'STEVE HALICKI', a race Joe Cordiano won. The Cambridge Times of 30 January 2004 calls the 2003 candidate Steve Halicki, so both forms of the name are used for that run. The York Guardian of 13 May 2005 calls the Conservative candidate Steve Halicki and says he ran for a federal seat unsuccessfully the previous summer, which is the 2004 run. The York Guardian's election story of 23 January 2006 lists Steve Halicki (Conservative), and the Etobicoke Guardian of 13 January 2006 lists Stephen Halicki for York South-Weston; both describe the held 2006 run, printed 'Steve Halicki'. The 2006 run also continues the 2004 run in the same office, riding and party at the next general election, under an uncommon surname with no other Halicki in the release. Steve is the usual short form of Stephen, and the sources use both forms for this candidate. The 2003 Ontario run, the 2004 federal run and the held 2006 federal run in York South—Weston are joined.

The Toronto Star's profiles of the York South—Weston candidates of 22 October 1993 describe the Natural Law candidate Greg Roberts as the driver of a transport truck. That is the 1993 York South—Weston Natural Law run printed Greg W. Roberts, fifth of eleven with 276 votes, and Elections Canada gives that candidate's occupation as truck driver. The Star's High Park ward list of 24 October 1994 names Nick Trainos, Myron Tymochko, Bill Roberts and Greg W. Roberts, all candidates in the 1994 former Toronto Ward 1 race, and its ward profiles of 10 November 1994 describe Greg Roberts as a truck driver and follower of Natural Law's teachings. That is the Ward 1 run printed Greg Roberts, sixth of six with 168 votes, and the list's form with the initial W. accounts for the record's form without it. The Star's High Park-Swansea profile of 5 June 1995 describes Greg W. Roberts, 48, of the Natural Law Party, as a transport driver who ran federally in 1993. That is the 1995 High Park-Swansea run, fifth of five with 286 votes, and the profile names the 1993 federal run. The Star's Parkdale—High Park coverage of 30 May 1997 names Gregory Wayne Roberts for the Natural Law Party, which is the 1997 Parkdale—High Park run, eighth of eight with 267 votes, and Elections Canada gives that candidate's occupation as transport driver, the occupation the Star gave in the same words for the 1995 candidate. Gregory Wayne is the full form of Greg W., and a source for each run attaches the same occupation to the short form and to the full form, which accounts for the different printed names. The four runs are in four different elections. Bill Roberts, who ran in the same 1994 ward, and Greg Robertson, the Canadian Action Party candidate in Parkdale—High Park in 2000, are separate Persons that these sources do not describe. The 1993 York South—Weston, 1994 Ward 1, 1995 High Park-Swansea and 1997 Parkdale—High Park runs are joined as one Person.

Wikipedia's page on the 1994 Toronto municipal election lists the Etobicoke Ward 12 council race as John Hastings 1,691, Vincent Crisanti 1,055, Adu K. Boakye 303 and Anil Banerjee 275. The candidates and totals are those of the City's record, which prints the runner-up as Vincent Chrisanti, so the page describes that run, spells the name Crisanti, and links it to its article on Vincent Crisanti, the later Ward 1 councillor, although the article itself begins his record with the 1997 Ward 5 race. The Globe and Mail's report on the 2010 Ward 1 (Etobicoke North) race, in which Crisanti unseated three-term councillor Suzan Hall, calls him "a former City of Etobicoke councillor". Hastings, already the incumbent in 1991, won Ward 12 in 1991 and 1994 and was elected to the legislature for Etobicoke-Rexdale in June 1995. The release's research notes on 1995 to 1997 vacancies record a Toronto Star editorial of 21 September 1995 saying that Etobicoke council appointed the runner-up from the 1994 vote to his seat instead of holding a by-election. That runner-up is the 1994 Ward 12 candidate, so the office the Globe gives for the 2010 winner matches the 1994 run, and Wikipedia's spelling shows the City's Chrisanti to be a misprint of Crisanti. No other Crisanti or Chrisanti appears in the release. The 1994 Etobicoke Ward 12 run is joined to the Person holding Vincent Crisanti's council runs from 1997 to 2026.

The Toronto Star of 23 May 1997, on the race for the new North York-Humber council ward, says 'Long-time North York school Trustee Bob Churchill is also registered, as is North York Ward 2 Councillor Gina Severino.' The Star's report card of 16 October 1997 lists Bob Churchill under Ward 6 North York-Humber. The record's 1997 Ward 6 field is Judy Sgro, George Mammoliti, Gina Severino (printed 'Gina Serverino'), Tony Marzilli, Michael Marson and a candidate printed 'Bob Churchhill', so the Star's Bob Churchill is that run and the City's 1997 table, which also misspells Severino, misprints his surname. The Star's description of him as a long-time North York school trustee matches the record's 1994 North York Board of Education Ward 2 run, which Bob Churchill won, so he was a sitting North York trustee when he registered. The 1994 North York Board of Education Ward 2 run and the 1997 Ward 6 council run are joined.

No source describes either candidate beyond the results, so the join rests on same-office continuity. The City's results give Michael Wiener third of four, with 3,897 votes, for Toronto District School Board trustee in Ward 11 in 2006, and Mike Wiener third of five, with 6,377 votes, in Ward 11 in 2010. Ward 11 was made up of city wards 21 and 22 (St. Paul's) at both elections, and the elections are consecutive. Mike is the common short form of Michael, so the printed names are forms of one name. Wiener is an uncommon surname: these are its only two runs in the release, and no other candidate of either printed name ran. The 2006 and 2010 Ward 11 trustee runs are joined as one Person.

Wikipedia's article on the 2006 Toronto municipal election profiles the mayoral candidate Mitch L. Gold, and its results table gives him 880 votes, which is the 2006 mayoral run (25th of 38, 880 votes). The profile says he was certified as a chartered accountant in 1968, that he unsuccessfully sought a seat on the Toronto Board of Education in 1994, and that he first ran for mayor of Toronto in 2003. The 2003 mayoral run is printed Mitch Gold (30th of 44, 412 votes). The only 1994 Toronto Board of Education run of the name in the release, and the only Gold on any 1994 school board ballot in it, is printed Mitchell Gold (Ward 11, City Wards 13 and 14, seventh of seven, 1,784 votes). The profile uses the short form Mitch for the man who ran in that 1994 race, which accounts for the different printed names, since Mitch is a common short form of Mitchell. The only other Gold in the release is Tao Gold, a 2000 council candidate. An earlier pass declined to link the 2006 run to the 2003 run on structure because a separate Person named Mitchell Gold existed; the profile shows that Person is the same man, so that reason no longer applies. The 1994 Toronto Board of Education Ward 11 run, the 2003 mayoral run and the 2006 mayoral run are joined as one Person.
